\caption{First-year outcomes in introductory courses and
  persistence, by subject, in the reference cohort. For each
  subject, the entrants holding a first attempt in a course
  numbered below 2000 during the first year are split by
  whether any such first attempt ended in a D, F, withdrawal, or
  no-credit outcome (DFW). Not observed later: no course record in
  a term one year or more after the entry term, through the end of
  the observation window (Section~\ref{sec:data:cohort}); an
  entrant who stopped out and returned counts as observed, and a
  transfer to another institution cannot be told from leaving
  higher education. The table uses the 8,837 entrants of the
  cohort (10,027) without the Coordinated Admission Program
  flag; the 1,190 entrants with the flag transfer after the
  first year by the design of that program. Parentheses hold
  pointwise 95\%
  intervals: a Wald interval for a difference, in percentage
  points, and the log (Woolf) method for the odds ratio. Subjects
  with at least 400 entrants holding such an attempt,
  ordered by the number with a DFW. An entrant can appear in
  several rows. The comparisons are unadjusted and exploratory:
  they were computed after the analysis plans were frozen, and
  the intervals are not adjusted for the number of subjects.}
